# TCS3472

m Color Light-to-Digital Converter with IR Filter

General Description The TCS3472 device provides a digital return of red, green, blue
(RGB), and clear light sensing values. An IR blocking filter,
integrated on-chip and localized to the color sensing
photodiodes, minimizes the IR spectral component of the
incoming light and allows color measurements to be made
accurately. The high sensitivity, wide dynamic range, and IR
blocking filter make the TCS3472 an ideal color sensor solution
for use under varying lighting conditions and through
attenuating materials.

The TCS3472 color sensor has a wide range of applications
including RGB LED backlight control, solid-state lighting,
health/fitness products, industrial process controls and medical
diagnostic equipment. In addition, the IR blocking filter enables
the TCS3472 to perform ambient light sensing (ALS). Ambient
light sensing is widely used in display-based products such as
cell phones, notebooks, and TVs to sense the lighting
environment and enable automatic display brightness for
optimal viewing and power savings. The TCS3472, itself, can
enter a lower-power wait state between light sensing
measurements to further reduce the average power
consumption.

_Ordering Information and Content Guide appear at end of_
_datasheet._

Key Benefits & Features

The benefits and features of TCS3472, Color Light-to-Digital
Converter with IR Filter are listed below:

 & \textbf{Detailed Description} \\
\hline
 & The TCS3472 light-to-digital converter contains a 3 x 4 photodiode array, four analog-to-digital converters (ADC) that integrate the photodiode current, data registers, a state machine, and an $I^2C$ interface. The 3 x 4 photodiode array is composed of red-filtered, green-filtered, blue-filtered, and clear (unfiltered) photodiodes. In addition, the photodiodes are coated with an IR-blocking filter. The four integrating ADCs simultaneously convert the amplified photodiode currents to a 16-bit digital value. Upon completion of a conversion cycle, the results are transferred to the data registers, which are double-buffered to ensure the integrity of the data. All of the internal timing, as well as the low-power wait state, is controlled by the state machine. \\

The response characteristics of the catalyst, in the present unit operation using liquid and vapor gases with and without a perforated distributive plate, are presented in Table 13. The performance is expressed as a function of correction of gas properties, expressed as the minimal mass flow rate of the raw material.

In the case of liquid, the minimum values of amine loading were 40% for water-like (impure) liquid and 60% liquid with 10 mol\% alkanol in water content. For saturation of the dilute phase, the correction factor increased respectively to 50% for pure ethylene glycol and 60% (20 mol\%) in the case of feeding with pure ethylene glycol. The corrections were relatively small and constant, and depended only on the correction factor. Fig. 13 presents graphically reported mass transfer performances as a function of correction, which allows comparison of changes for which it is possible to provide an indication on their impact.

Values of correction obtained for both liquid and vapor streams for the whole test range of amine loading, carrying no work by the gas mixture and with gas flow, are reasonably reproducible (2-3)-% variation of correction.

In the case of the vapor, the correction ranged from 28% to 47% (or from 0.71 to 0.91).

As expected for these liquid and vapor series, the mass transfer coefficient is influenced by at least three working parameters. Variation in their values, in the range of 5-10% (or from 0.09 to 0.20) is sufficient to change the mass transfer coefficient of a given amine-desorption step (< 10\%). The minimal rates of performance increases (< 4\%) corresponds to the gain (< 5\%) in the weight rate of an amine-desorption step and to the gain of 10\%) of the desorption rate (< 1\%).

**Example Light sources and spectra**

At the start of each spectral responsivity measurement, a known LED source is squared into a pulse width of between 100 and 200ns. A broadband LED that emits another set of 200 to 1200nm spectra is applied for about 5ms at a minimum red irradiance of less than 1W/cm[2] without disrupting the results with a filament. This corresponds to the OID budget of each pixel using two LED configurations; one with a handheld power source at 20cm from the diode and the other from 50cm, and the PMS as in Figure 3. Normalizing spectra to per level, the pulse preamplifiers are mounted at full scale. The MFFST Gatinet in Figure 13 also shows the McGurk effect at around 600nm Figure 13: This is fitted with the resulting demodulator polynomial temperature and power calibrated from the pixel sensitivity of the field of view experiment adjusted for a constant spectral responsivity. Using conditions that tend to be unique for the Gatinet, results may deviate from this being well beyond 400nm as the coating of silicon in this application does not reflect the nearly isotropic 680nm reflection.

} - 已成为当今数字图像设计中从设计工具转移到DIC/M优于的其他标准【13】。然而，考虑到对生物活性的研究正在引领显微镜的进一步发展，从而将TMDs嵌入材料本质上具有生物活性的特征和其他性能的参数。例如，许多TMDs可以以 আপনি be条件下起作用，例如加剧低温度下的细胞活性，因此称为温度响应材料。此外，溪流，其中许多TMDs展示了环境响应特性，可以按照胡桃作为生物平台【14】。在诸如液态或气态环境的温度不同的情况下，TMDs的独特特性可通过利用DIC或MPM参数从全球角度来看进行显着修改，其中这些参数是根据所涉及的环境参数计算出的光学常数(透镜、孔径、视场等)。最近，由于诸如活细胞中草药提取物在内的环境参数正在影响DIC和MPM时，对TMD的微观理解亟待提高。
